geometry_edits.rationale: Shift from a generic box to a more articulated plan-based prism so the mass can support a stronger courtyard/bar relationship.
Slightly increase section presence so the carved court and upper massing read more clearly in profile.
Move the approach cut to the street-facing corner to reinforce the entrance seam toward access.
Deepen the corner cut so the entry condition is visible as a real massing event.
Enlarge the court void to improve publicness and make the access edge semantically active.
Maintain an open court facing the verified access side so the public threshold remains legible.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the neutral box datum with a more program-responsive base mass that can read as a compact bar/slab instead of a generic extrusion.
Broaden the primary mass slightly to support a more legible street-building presence and reduce the boxy standalone object feel.
Retarget the corner cut to better align the public approach with the verified access edge and strengthen the oblique entry gesture.
Make the corner removal more assertive so the access response is clearly read as a street threshold rather than a minor trim.
Increase the carved court proportion to improve public void legibility and give the frontage a more meaningful open-space figure.
Keep the void explicitly open to the access side so the ground response remains aligned with the verified street edge.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact U-shaped slab with one carved opening, so it has a recognizable dominant gesture and a basic public-void idea. However, the mass is still semantically weak for neighborhood living because the street response is only partially legible, the open edge feels more like an incised notch than an active ground threshold, and the section remains almost completely flat/box-like. Across the four views the form is coherent enough and the parcel containment appears respected, but the silhouette is too generic and the void lacks enough public character to carry the program contract strongly. It is closer to an abstract courtyard block than to a mixed-use street building with a clearly activated frontage and meaningful upper/ground hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is low-rise retail/hospitality rather than the candidate’s U-shaped courtyard slab; useful for active frontage, not for copying form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact pavilion-like street edge with a clear ground threshold and a small attached vertical/service element can support neighborhood-scale mixed use.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The waterfront megastructure and pronounced stepped sections are much larger and more complex than this compact neighborhood-living candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Strong courtyard/terrace logic and linear bar massing show how public void and upper hierarchy can coexist in a neighborhood program.

warnings: The thin blue frontage edge appears to be answered indirectly rather than with a strong public threshold or entry seam.
The section is very shallow and does not yet express a programmatic roof/void relationship beyond basic subtraction.
No obvious cross-view collision is visible, and parcel containment appears satisfied from the image set.
